author: smimon
text:
keen246 wrote: I just finished this journal. It was indeed a great learning experience. I just can help wondering why people who are doing great on their threads/journals suddenly disappear without a trace. Is it because they became so proficient and no longer feel the need to discuss on the forums? Is it because they realized making money on Forex is too hard and stop trying? Is it because they concluded the markets are not for them? Is it because...?

Not to wish to speak on behalf of DrSwing, but I believe it's because documenting your thoughts and trying to teach others is a cathartic part of one's own learning process.

Once you feel near to attaining a level of mastery, the urge to journal everything and constantly comment on the posts of others evaporates somewhat. I presume the majority of good traders on here who were writing regularly updated journals, and then stopped, simply reached the natural end of their journey, and lost the compulsion to write updates any more. Perhaps some went on to other things - but I'm not sure how many people would, after devoting months and years to learning a very difficult discipline which is essentially a license to print money, would totally stop doing it, unless they were simply in it for the intellectual challenge.
